/preschool-tuition-reminders.description: Schedule preschool tuition reminder texts for monthly due dates. Organize families by classroom, review PAID replies and verify payments. See plans and a free demo.
/preschool-tuition-reminders.heading: Preschool tuition reminders that fit your monthly routine.
/preschool-tuition-reminders.intro: Keep monthly tuition follow-up organized across your preschool classrooms. TuitionPing schedules before-due, due-date and overdue text reminders using each family's tuition amount and monthly due day. Parents use their usual text-message app and can reply PAID. Your team checks the payment records and confirms receipt in the dashboard.
/preschool-tuition-reminders.pains_heading: Give the office a repeatable tuition routine
pains: Different classrooms, one review process
Organize families by classroom and location. Review the tuition records you maintain before following up, including different amounts for part-time attendance and approved arrangements.
A message between drop-off and pickup
An ordinary text gives a family a clear amount, due date and payment instruction. Parents can reply from their phone without a TuitionPing account or app.
A payment report waiting to be checked
PAID tells your team that a parent reports sending money. Check the amount and billing period in your bank or payment-service records before confirming receipt and stopping that period's follow-ups.
/preschool-tuition-reminders.buying_heading: Check the fit for your preschool
buying_points: The reminder subscription follows monthly due-day schedules. The free invoice generator and tracker also work with manually entered weekly or term dates; those tools do not add weekly or term automation to the subscription.
The payment method in your agreement

Continue accepting the checks, transfers or other payment method you already use. TuitionPing schedules texts and records replies. Your staff still handles reconciliation, partial payments and credits in your records.

Before a break, new term or enrollment change, review amounts, monthly due days and which families should receive reminders. The app does not automatically read your preschool calendar, prorate tuition or adjust bills for holidays.
/preschool-tuition-reminders.workflow_heading: Set up your preschool's monthly follow-up
steps: Prepare the family roster
Add your location and classrooms, then enter families or use the existing CSV family import. Record the correct tuition amount, monthly due day, contact details and permission for tuition texts.
Review your message wording
Include the payment instructions from your enrollment agreement and check the before-due, due-date and overdue templates. Choose English or Spanish for each family's messages.
Preview and send a test text
Use the setup wizard to preview the message and send your test text. Check the program name, amount, date and instructions before relying on the schedule.
Verify payment reports
When a parent replies PAID, check your actual payment records. Confirm only the payments you have verified. Keep the spreadsheet or bookkeeping system you use for credits and reconciliation.
/preschool-tuition-reminders.example_heading: Example: monthly tuition across two preschool classrooms
/preschool-tuition-reminders.example: Little Oak Preschool has 24 families across its morning and full-day classrooms. One family's monthly tuition is $600 and due on the 1st; a second family has a different amount due on the 15th. Staff enter each family's own details, then preview the wording: ‘Little Oak Preschool: Tuition of $600 is due on November 1. Please use the payment method in your enrollment agreement and reply PAID once sent.’ A PAID reply moves the record into payment review. The office checks its payment records and confirms receipt. Before the winter break, staff review the next month's tuition and reminder settings against the school's agreement.
/preschool-tuition-reminders.example_note: Fictional preschool, families and amounts. Scheduled reminders do not prove message reading or payment receipt. Your agreement determines the actual charges and dates.
/preschool-tuition-reminders.fit_heading: A focused option for an existing billing process
/preschool-tuition-reminders.fit: This workflow fits a preschool that already has a way to bill families and receive tuition, and wants consistent monthly text follow-up. Attendance, enrollment, online tuition collection, automatic bank reconciliation and school-calendar billing require other tools. The public demo lets you try the reminder, parent reply and provider-confirmation sequence before choosing a plan.
faq: Can preschool families have different tuition amounts and due days?
Yes. Set each family's tuition amount and monthly due day on its record. Review those settings when enrollment, attendance arrangements or your agreement changes.
Do parents need to install an app?
No. Parents receive ordinary text messages and can reply PAID from their normal text-message app. Staff use the TuitionPing dashboard.
Does TuitionPing collect preschool tuition?
No. Keep your existing payment method. A parent's PAID reply is a report; your team checks the actual payment records and confirms receipt.
Does it support weekly, term or holiday-adjusted billing automatically?

The reminder subscription uses monthly due-day schedules. It does not automatically apply your school calendar or prorate charges. The free spreadsheet and document generator accept manually entered dates for other billing schedules.
Which plan should a preschool choose?

Choose by the total families and locations on your account. A preschool with 24 families at one location fits Starter. The pricing page shows current monthly and annual prices, family limits and trial terms.
Can I try it before creating an account?

Yes. The public demo uses fictional families, needs no account or card and sends no texts. The real 30-day trial requires a card at secure checkout, with the selected subscription starting afterward unless you cancel.

/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.description: Send daycare tuition reminder texts in each family's preferred English or Spanish. Preview bilingual examples, customize wording and verify payment reports.
/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.example: English: ‘Sunshine Daycare: Tuition of $1,200 is due today, October 8. Please use our usual payment method and reply PAID once you have sent it.’ The Spanish version carries the same amount, the same date and the same next step — a family can put the two side by side and get one message. The same pairing exists for the heads-up before the due date and for the follow-ups at three and seven days late. If the Spanish version and the English version ever seemed to disagree, the family has still received one clear amount and one clear date — because both templates come from the same family record, not from two separate lists kept in two languages.
/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.example_heading: The same due-day reminder, two clear versions
/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.example_note: Fictional example. PAID is the reply keyword shown here; payment still requires provider verification. STOP opts out of texts.
faq: Can English and Spanish families be in the same classroom?
Yes. The reminder language is set per family, rather than requiring a separate classroom. Families in the same room can receive different languages on the same schedule.
Can I edit the Spanish wording?

Yes. Both template sets are editable. Check that the meaning matches your English version and your written agreement — TuitionPing does not auto-translate, so your approved wording is exactly what goes out.
What do parents reply?
The same short keywords in both languages: PAID to report a payment, BAL for a balance, ABSENT for an absence, STOP to opt out. The Spanish templates spell out what each reply means, in Spanish.
Is the dashboard in Spanish too?
No. Signup and the staff dashboard are in English. What switches language is everything the families receive — reminders, follow-ups and statements — which is where comprehension matters most.
Are the bilingual templates free?
Yes. The downloadable English and Spanish reminder templates are free, with no signup required. Automated messaging is part of TuitionPing's paid service after its trial.
Can I read this page in Spanish?
Yes — this same page is available in Spanish: busca el enlace a la versión en español en los recursos de esta página. (Look for the Spanish-version link in this page's resources.)
Is there a Spanish version of this site?
Yes. The Spanish landing page explains the same service in Spanish — look for “Lee esta página en español” in this page's resources. The free reminder templates are bilingual too.
/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.fit: One program can have families receiving English reminders and others receiving Spanish reminders, in the same classroom and on the same schedule. This feature concerns the text messages; it does not promise a fully Spanish-language staff dashboard or interpretation services — signup and the provider dashboard are in English, while the family-facing texts are what switch. Review the wording with someone familiar with your families and program policies.

/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.heading: Send tuition reminders in the language each family prefers.
/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.intro: A useful tuition reminder needs to be understandable: the amount, due date, payment method and next step should be clear the first time a parent reads it. When reminders go out in only one language, some parents are left decoding the most important message your program sends — the one about money. TuitionPing lets you choose English or Spanish for each family and edit the reminder templates in both languages, so every family gets the same clear message in the language they actually read. The result is fewer misunderstandings about the message every family cares about most.
/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.kicker: For programs serving English- and Spanish-speaking families
pains: One language, quietly ignored

A reminder written only in English may be skimmed or misunderstood by a Spanish-dominant parent — not from unwillingness to pay, but because the amount, date or payment method never landed. The late payment looks like a money problem when it was a communication problem.
Translated on the fly, differently every time

Asking a bilingual staff member to translate reminders in the moment produces a different message each month, and a wrong digit in an amount or date is worse than no translation at all. Saved templates keep both versions consistent.
Parents who won't ask for clarification

Many parents won't admit they didn't understand a message in their second language — especially about money. A clear text in their preferred language, with a simple reply keyword, removes the need to ask.
Two households, two languages

In many families one parent reads English and the other reads Spanish. Because the language is set per family rather than per program, each family's reminders arrive in the language that household chose — while their English-reading neighbors get English. The reminder lands in the language the household actually reads at the kitchen table.
/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.pains_heading: Where bilingual tuition follow-up breaks down
resources: Download English and Spanish text templates
/bilingual-daycare-tuition-reminders.spanish: Español: ‘Sunshine Daycare: Su pago de $1,200 vence hoy, 8 de octubre. Use nuestro método de pago habitual y responda PAID cuando haya enviado el pago.’
steps: Ask the family which language they prefer

Record the preference on the family's contact details. Do not infer it from a name. Obtain permission for tuition texts and explain how replies and opt-outs work — in the language the family prefers, whenever you can.
Review both sets of templates

Customize English and Spanish wording to match your program's agreement. Keep amounts, dates, payment instructions and late-fee terms consistent across languages, so neither version promises anything the other doesn't.
Preview before you send

Check a sample message for the correct family, amount and date. Avoid abbreviations that make the next action unclear. The public demo lets you switch languages on the same sample reminder to compare both versions side by side.
Keep the written policy bilingual too

Send the enrollment agreement and late-fee policy in both languages, so the reminder texts point back to terms the family has already seen and understood. A reminder should never be the first place a family meets your late fee. The free late-fee policy template on this site is a starting point for the English version; have the Spanish version reviewed by someone you trust before you rely on it.
Separate a report from a receipt
Explain that replying PAID tells the provider to check the records. Verify the payment before treating it as received, regardless of the language of the original reminder.

/home-daycare-tuition-reminders.buying_heading: Choosing a payment reminder app for your home daycare
buying_points: You use the TuitionPing dashboard; families use their normal text-message app. A parent can reply PAID, and you check your records before confirming receipt. The reply reports a payment; it is not a bank confirmation.
Keep the way families already pay

Accept the checks, cash or payment service covered by your agreement. Include clear payment instructions in your reminder wording. TuitionPing does not move money or provide an automatic connection to those services.

The paid reminder service follows monthly due-day schedules. If you bill weekly, use the free reminder generator or payment tracker for that workflow, and check the service's supported settings before subscribing.
/home-daycare-tuition-reminders.example: One family's monthly tuition is due on the 5th and another's on the 10th. A part-time family owes a smaller amount on the 15th. Put their own dates and amounts on their records, and each family gets its own schedule — no group text, no crossed wires. A due-day text can say: ‘Hi Alex, tuition of $800 for Little Oak Daycare is due today. Please use our usual payment method and reply PAID once sent.’ You still check your records before verifying payment. If the family on the 10th pays by check at pickup on the 9th, you mark it verified and that family's follow-ups stop — the other family's schedule is untouched. Nothing about one family's payment changes what anyone else receives.

faq: Do parents need another app?
No. Parents receive ordinary text messages and can reply from any phone. They do not need a TuitionPing parent account, a download, or a login.
Can I keep taking checks or transfers?
Yes. TuitionPing handles reminders and parent replies. You continue using your existing payment method — check, transfer, cash, or the app you already use — and verify receipt yourself.
How much does it cost for a home daycare?
The Micro plan is $9/month for up to 10 families at one location, and every plan starts with a 30-day free trial. A card is collected at signup but is not charged during the trial.
Can both parents get the reminder?
Yes. Add a second parent's phone number and both numbers receive the texts. Either parent can reply PAID, and the reply is recorded against the same family.
Can I pause reminders for one family?
Yes. Each family can be paused (snoozed) until a date you set — useful for vacations or a payment arrangement you have already made — while everyone else's reminders continue normally.
Can I start with the free tracker instead?

Yes. The tuition payment tracker works independently of TuitionPing. It helps organize balances but does not send reminders. Many home providers start there and switch to automatic texts when the hand-texting gets old.
What if a parent doesn't have a smartphone?
Any phone that can receive text messages works, including a basic flip phone. Parents do not need internet access, an app, or a data plan to get a reminder or reply PAID.

pains: You are the entire office

Cooking, cleaning, licensing paperwork, nap schedules and parent updates already fill the day. Reminder texts compete with all of it, so they go out late, in a rush, or not at all — and tuition quietly slips a week.
Every family is on a different rhythm

One family pays monthly on the 1st, another started mid-month, a third is part-time with a smaller amount. Holding six different due dates, amounts and arrangements in your head works until the first busy week. Miss one family's date and you have sent a reminder for a payment that is not due yet — the fastest way to teach parents to ignore your texts.
Asking face-to-face is the hard part

You see these parents every morning and every evening. Asking about an overdue payment at pickup, in front of other families, is awkward for everyone. A polite text sent by a system keeps the relationship warm and the business part separate.
Hand-texting the same message eight times

Copying the same reminder to each family, one phone at a time, after cleanup and dishes, is exactly the kind of small repeated task that gets skipped when you're tired — and it's the task that gets you paid on time.
/home-daycare-tuition-reminders.pains_heading: Where tuition follow-up breaks down for home providers
steps: Write down the agreement

Give each family the amount, due date, payment method and any late-fee terms before enrollment. A reminder reinforces that agreement; it does not replace it. Families who know the date and the fee rarely need the third reminder.
Enter each family's details

Add the parent contact, tuition amount and due date, then choose English or Spanish. Obtain permission for tuition texts before adding a phone number. A second parent's number can be added so both caregivers see the reminder.
Let the schedule handle follow-up

The app schedules a heads-up three days before the due date, a due-day reminder, and unpaid follow-ups at three and seven days overdue. Customize the message wording to sound like your program, and set quiet hours so texts arrive at reasonable times.
Pause when life happens

A family on vacation, a payment already arranged, a temporary hardship you have agreed on — pause (snooze) reminders for that family until a date you choose, so nobody gets nudged about a balance you have already discussed.
Check your actual receipts

Review checks, transfers or the payment platform you already use. A parent replying PAID records a report for review. Mark the tuition paid after you confirm receipt — the reply starts the check, it does not replace it.

buying_points: A roster your office can maintain

Import families from CSV and organize them by classroom and location. Check amounts, monthly due days and phone numbers before sending. You manage the account through one owner login; the service does not provide separate staff roles.

Review parent PAID replies alongside your payment records, then confirm receipt. Message history records sending activity and replies; it does not establish that a parent read a message or that funds reached your bank.
The right scope for your center

Choose scheduled SMS follow-up when your billing and payment process already works. If you need weekly automated billing, attendance, enrollment or integrated payment processing, check a broader platform against those requirements.
/small-daycare-tuition-reminders.example: A center has an infant room and a preschool room, 24 families in all. Most pay on the 1st; a few mid-month starters pay on the 15th. Organize both rosters by classroom, while preserving each family's own tuition amount and due date. At the office check, review parent payment reports against your payment platform, verify the receipts that match, and privately follow up on unresolved balances. When a parent says they never got a reminder, the message log shows the dates and times each text went out. Over a month, the daily check replaces the end-of-month scramble — open balances get seen every day instead of once, while they are still small and easy to resolve.

faq: Can I organize families by classroom?
Yes. Families are organized under classrooms and locations. Keep the contact details and tuition schedule accurate for each family, and each classroom's roster stays separate in the dashboard.
Does TuitionPing collect tuition?

No. TuitionPing sends reminders and records replies. Your existing payment method collects the tuition, and you verify receipt. That separation is deliberate: no new payment system for parents to learn.
How long does it take to set a center up?
Most centers import their roster by CSV in one sitting, then customize the message wording. The four reminder stages run automatically after that — there is no per-month setup to repeat.
What happens when a parent opts out?
A parent can reply STOP to stop texts. Use an appropriate alternative for tuition communication with that family and update the family's records rather than repeatedly texting them.
Can we run two locations on one account?
Yes, on the Growth plan and above, which covers up to 75 families across unlimited locations. Each location keeps its own classrooms, payment link and late-fee settings.
Who on staff runs it?
TuitionPing uses one owner account rather than separate staff roles. In practice the director or office manager runs the short daily check; the reminders themselves need no one to send them.
Can I set different late fees for different locations?
Yes. The late-fee amount and timing are set per location, and each location keeps its own payment link, so a second site's families see that site's terms.

pains: Three lists that never match

The roster sits in one system, payments land in another, and the reminder list lives in someone's email or notebook. Reconciling the three by hand, every month, is where late balances hide for weeks. Each source is a little out of date in a different way, so nobody fully trusts any of them.
The routine walks out the door
When the assistant director who 'always handled billing' leaves, the follow-up rhythm leaves with her. A documented, automatic schedule keeps running through staff changes, vacations and flu season.
“Nobody told me” has no answer

A parent insists they were never reminded. Without a message log, that conversation is your word against theirs. A timestamped record of every text sent and every reply received settles it in seconds.
Evenings of one-by-one data entry
Typing the same reminder to thirty families, or re-entering a roster you already keep elsewhere, burns director hours. A CSV import brings the roster in once, and the schedule does the repeating.

steps: Prepare a clean roster

Use a CSV import or enter families individually. Check the parent phone number, amount, due date and classroom. One accurate record is more useful than separate reminder lists in several inboxes. Clean data matters more than speed here: one wrong digit in a phone number means a reminder that never arrives and a family that never knew.
Set the program's message wording

Use a consistent explanation of the due date and payment method. Customize before-due, due-day and overdue messages in English and Spanish, and configure quiet hours for your timezone so families are never texted at 6 a.m.
Run the daily office check

Make it a ten-minute morning habit: open the dashboard, review which families replied PAID, which balances are still open, and which follow-ups went out. The check replaces the monthly scramble with a small daily glance.
Review replies in the dashboard
Parents can reply PAID. Treat those replies as a review queue, then compare them with the center's payment records. Message history helps you see what was sent and received, family by family.
Finish reconciliation

Confirm the actual payment before marking tuition paid. Keep bookkeeping and tuition receipts in the records your center already uses. The reminder system does not verify bank deposits, and a PAID reply is a report to check — not proof of payment.
